featured_reviews.name: pritpal singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been donating to Nanhri Pari Foundation for a long time and have always contributed according to my financial capacity. While I genuinely appreciate the work they do, I am extremely disappointed with the recent experience.

For the last six months, I have been receiving repeated WhatsApp messages pressuring me to make “urgent” donations. This constant follow-up feels intrusive and uncomfortable. Donations should always be voluntary and made from the heart ,not solicited through repeated or forceful requests.

I truly hope the organisation reviews this approach. Respecting donors’ boundaries is essential for maintaining trust and long-term support. If the communication style does not improve, it becomes difficult for genuine supporters like me to continue contributing.

featured_reviews.name: Chirag Laheru
featured_reviews.review_text:
We provided social media management services to Nanhi Pari Foundation in good faith, but after partial payment and using the whole service , they ghosted us despite repeated reminders for the remaining payment. It’s disappointing when an NGO, which should uphold trust and integrity, exploits freelancers/small businesses.

If you’re working with them, ensure agreements are in writing. Transparency matters, especially for organisations claiming to drive social change. Hope they rectify this, as such behavior undermines their credibility.

featured_reviews.name: Joel Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: We were scammed by the Nanhi Pari Foundation. Despite delivering everything as per our contract, they completely ghosted us when it came time for payment. Numerous calls, emails, and messages went unanswered. I strongly advise others not to engage with them especially if you are a freelancer or small business relying on timely payments.

featured_reviews.name: MEET G PAREKH
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dishonest & Unreliable
We provided social media management services to Nanhi Pari Foundation, but they refused to release the final payment despite completing the work. It’s shocking that an NGO, which should operate with integrity, would exploit service providers like this.
Stay cautious of dealing with them

featured_reviews.name: Aser Media
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a professional social media agency, we partnered with Nanhi Pari Foundation in good faith, delivering high-quality services as agreed. However, despite multiple assurances, they failed to honor their financial obligations, withholding a significant portion of the payment without justification.
What’s most concerning is their complete lack of communication—emails and reminders were ignored, demonstrating a blatant disregard for ethical business conduct. For an organization that claims to champion social causes, this behavior is hypocritical and damaging to their credibility.

Ø Surgery Support Program (SSP): It provides direct financial aid to underserved children needing critical medical treatment for their health and well-being. Since inception it has helped to save lives of more than 9000+ children across 23 States in India.

name: Swades Foundation | Rural Empowerment
description: Swades Foundation, One of the Top NGOS in India working for rural empowerment. It works in four main areas of development which are Water & Sanitation, Health, Education and Livelihoods. This includes providing each home with access to a drinking water tap inside the house, an individual toilet, making primary healthcare accessible to the villagers, providing scholarships and faculties for school infrastructure, livelihood opportunities etc. In the year 2022, Swades Foundation has completed 75 dream villages project. A village qualifies as a Swades Dream Village by achieving over 40 parameters bucketed into 5 S's : Swachh(Clean),Sundar(Beautiful),Swasthya(Access to Healthcare),Sakshar(Educated) and Saksham(Self-Reliant)

featured_reviews.name: Pooja Yagnik
featured_reviews.review_text:
I have been immensely impressed by the Swades Foundation's work and their unwavering commitment to making a real difference in rural and tribal communities. Their work is not just genuine, but it's transformative. The impact they've had on the lives of those in need is nothing short of remarkable.

What sets Swades Foundation apart is their laser-focused goal – improving the lives of those living in underserved areas. This clarity of purpose ensures that every initiative, every project is meticulously designed to address the most pressing issues faced by these communities, be it Drinking water, sanitation, education, healthcare, or livelihood opportunities.

One of the standout features of Swades Foundation is their enthusiastic and dedicated team and management. Their passion for the cause is palpable, and it reflects in the results they achieve. They don't just implement projects; they invest in the empowerment of the people they serve.

In summary, Swades Foundation is a shining example of an organization that not only talks the talk but walks the walk. They are creating tangible, life-changing impacts, and their commitment to their mission is truly inspiring. This is the kind of organization that makes the world a better place, one rural and tribal life at a time. Kudos to the Swades Foundation!

featured_reviews.name: Eknath Chandrakant Pawar
featured_reviews.review_text:
ABOUT PRAJA

Praja is a non-partisan organisation working towards enabling accountable governance since 1999. Praja empowers citizens to participate in governance by providing knowledge and perspective so that they can become politically active and involved beyond the ballot box. It undertakes extensive research and highlights civic issues to build the awareness of, and mobilize action by the government and elected representatives (ERs).

THE PROBLEM

Praja believes that uninformed and disengaged ERs and administration, rather than existing systems or policies, are responsible for the lack of good governance. There is a paucity of tools to facilitate effective interaction between citizens and the local government.

PRAJA's RESPONSE

Praja conducts data driven research and provides information on civic issues to citizens, media, and government administration and works with ERs to identify and address inefficiencies in their work processes, bridge the information gaps, and help them in taking corrective measures.

HOW DID IT EVOLVE?

1999: Praja, along with the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), created Mumbai's first Citizen Charter
2003: Teamed up with BMC and built its citizens' grievance redressal mechanism, the Online Complaint and Management System (OCMS), and conducted complaint audits in the ensuing years
2005: Published Mumbai Citizen's Handbook to demystify governance in Mumbai; About 2 lakh copies distributed
2008: Initiated Praja Dialogue; launched CityScan, an online collation of extensive data on civic and security Issues In Mumbai; Published councillor handbook; and annual report cards on MLAs, and councillors
2014: Conducted workshops with ERs, educating them on policies and roles; started the Delhi Chapter to replicate the model developed In Mumbai
2016: Launched MLA and Councillor Report Cards in Delhi
